rv.q: Peyankov and team have skillfully harnessed the resources of a storefront theater to make Beckett’s “corpsed” world feel utterly real.

This rendition is much funnier than I remember but we as a culture are much closer to living this nightmare than the last time I saw this show, so this masterful cast is able to hit closer to the bone.
Peyankov and his ensemble clearly understand Beckett's bleeding heart, something often ignored or dismissed when talking about Beckett's wily work.
Facility Theatre continues to impress with another in a long line of brave and transformative productions.

cn.t: Facility Theatre's production of Beckett's "Endgame" earns strong praise for its pitch-perfect performances and timely resonance, mapping post-WWII existential dread onto today's climate anxieties with stark, effective staging.
